name: jira_add_comment
title: Add Comment
description: Add a comment to a Jira issue.

public.description: (Optional) For JSM/Service Desk issues only. Set to true for customer-visible comment, false for internal agent-only comment. Posted via the ServiceDesk API as a raw string; Jira Cloud renders it server-side and stores ADF (markdown observed to render on Cloud, without the client-side markdown-to-ADF guarantees of the regular comment path). Cannot be combined with visibility. If the issue's project is listed in JIRA_INTERNAL_ONLY_PROJECTS, only public=false is accepted — public=true or omitting this field is rejected.

name: jira_add_issues_to_sprint
title: Add Issues to Sprint
description: Add issues to a Jira sprint.

sprint_id.description: Sprint ID to add issues to

name: jira_create_issue
title: Create Issue
description: Create a new Jira issue with optional Epic link or parent for subtasks.

project_key.description: The JIRA project key (e.g. 'PROJ', 'DEV', 'ACV2'). This is the prefix of issue keys in your project. Never assume what it might be, always ask the user.

issue_type.description: Issue type (e.g. 'Task', 'Bug', 'Story', 'Epic', 'Subtask'). The available types depend on your project configuration. For subtasks, use 'Subtask' (not 'Sub-task') and include parent in additional_fields.

assignee.description: (Optional) Assignee's user identifier (string): Email, display name, or account ID (e.g., 'user@example.com', 'John Doe', 'accountid:...')

description.description: Issue description in Markdown format. On Jira Cloud, use '{expand:Title}...{expand}' for a collapsible section.

components.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of component names to assign (e.g., 'Frontend,API')

name: jira_create_issue_link
title: Create Issue Link
description: Create a link between two Jira issues.

link_type.description: The type of link to create (e.g., 'Duplicate', 'Blocks', 'Relates to')

inward_issue_key.description: The key of the inward issue (e.g., 'PROJ-123', 'ACV2-642')

outward_issue_key.description: The key of the outward issue (e.g., 'PROJ-456')

comment.description: (Optional) Comment to add to the link. Rejected when either linked issue belongs to a project listed in JIRA_INTERNAL_ONLY_PROJECTS (a link comment may be customer-visible on JSM and cannot be forced internal): create the link without a comment, then post an internal note with jira_add_comment(public=false) on the relevant issue.

comment_visibility.description: (Optional) Visibility settings for the comment as JSON string (e.g. '{"type":"group","value":"jira-users"}')

name: jira_get_agile_boards
title: Get Agile Boards
description: Get jira agile boards by name, project key, or type.

board_name.description: (Optional) The name of board, support fuzzy search

name: jira_get_all_projects
title: Get All Projects
description: Get all Jira projects accessible to the current user.

include_archived.description: Whether to include archived projects in the results

name: jira_get_board_issues
title: Get Board Issues
description: Get all issues linked to a specific board filtered by JQL.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

expand.description: Optional fields to expand in the response (e.g., 'changelog').

name: jira_get_create_fields
title: Get Create Fields
description:
Get fields available for creating an issue of a specific type.

Returns all fields (required and optional) for the given project and
issue type, including field names, IDs, whether they're required, and
their schema. Use jira_get_field_options when a returned field needs its
allowed values.

issue_type_id.description: The issue type ID (from get_project_issue_types). Example: '10002' for Task.

name: jira_get_issue
title: Get Issue
description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue.

Includes Epic links and relationship information. Use the
``include`` parameter to inline enrichments (remote_links,
transitions, watchers, changelog, comments, worklogs) so that
separate tool calls are not needed.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

include.description: (Optional) Comma-separated sections to inline in the response, avoiding extra tool calls. Supported: all, remote_links, transitions, watchers, changelog, comments, worklogs

use_display_names.description: When true, custom field keys in the output use human-readable display names (e.g. 'Story Points') instead of opaque IDs (e.g. 'customfield_10243'). The 'names' expansion is added automatically. Standard fields are unaffected.

name: jira_get_link_types
title: Get Link Types
description: Get all available issue link types.

name_filter.description: (Optional) Filter link types by name substring (case-insensitive)

name: jira_get_project_fields
title: Get Project Fields
description:
Get the fields available on issues of a project (the create schema),
deduplicated across the project's issue types — i.e. which fields tickets in
this project have, regardless of whether they are filled.

name: jira_get_project_issue_types
title: Get Project Issue Types
description:
Get available issue types for a Jira project.

Returns the list of issue types (Bug, Task, Story, Epic, etc.) that can
be created in the specified project. Use the returned issue type IDs with
get_create_fields to discover what fields each type requires.

name: jira_get_sprint_issues
title: Get Sprint Issues
description: Get jira issues from sprint.

fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

name: jira_get_sprints_from_board
title: Get Sprints from Board
description: Get jira sprints from board by state.

name: jira_get_transitions
title: Get Transitions
description: Get available status transitions for a Jira issue.

name: jira_get_user_profile
title: Get User Profile
description: Retrieve profile information for a specific Jira user.

user_identifier.description: Identifier for the user (e.g., email address 'user@example.com', username 'johndoe', account ID 'accountid:...', or key for Server/DC).

name: jira_search
title: Search Issues
description: Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

use_display_names.description: When true, custom field keys in the output use human-readable display names (e.g. 'Story Points') instead of opaque IDs (e.g. 'customfield_10243'). The 'names' expansion is added automatically. Standard fields are unaffected.

name: jira_search_assignable_users
title: Search Assignable Users
description:
Search Jira users assignable in a given project or issue.

Use this when you have a display name / partial name / email fragment
and need a concrete identifier (``name`` / ``key`` for Server/DC,
``accountId`` for Cloud) to feed into assignee, reporter, watcher, etc.

Returns the full result set so the caller can disambiguate when several
users match — ``get_user_profile`` only resolves one identifier and is
not designed for human-name search.

Exactly one of ``project_key`` or ``issue_key`` must be provided — the
underlying API (``/user/assignable/search``) requires a project or issue
context and works without the global "Browse Users" permission that bot
accounts in locked-down DC instances often lack.

query.description: Free-form text to search Jira users by: display name, username, or email substring (e.g. 'Smith', 'jane.doe', 'doe@example.com'). Server-side match is case-insensitive and partial.

project_key.description: Project key to scope the search to (e.g. 'DT'). Required if issue_key is not given.

issue_key.description: Issue key to scope the search to (e.g. 'DT-779'). Required if project_key is not given.

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return (default 20).

name: jira_search_fields
title: Search Fields
description: Search Jira fields by keyword with fuzzy match.

keyword.description: Keyword for fuzzy search. If left empty, lists the first 'limit' available fields in their default order.

refresh.description: Whether to force refresh the field list

name: jira_transition_issue
title: Transition Issue
description: Transition a Jira issue to a new status.

transition_id.description: ID of the transition to perform. Use the jira_get_transitions tool first to get the available transition IDs for the issue. Example values: '11', '21', '31'

fields.description: (Optional) JSON string of fields to update during the transition. Some transitions require specific fields to be set (e.g., resolution). Example: '{"resolution": {"name": "Fixed"}}'

comment.description: (Optional) Comment to add during the transition in Markdown format. This will be visible in the issue history. Rejected for projects listed in JIRA_INTERNAL_ONLY_PROJECTS (a transition comment may be customer-visible on JSM and cannot be forced internal): transition without a comment, then post an internal note with jira_add_comment(public=false).

name: jira_update_issue
title: Update Issue
description: Update an existing Jira issue including changing status, adding Epic links, updating fields, etc.

fields.description: JSON string of fields to update. For 'assignee', provide a string identifier (email, name, or accountId). For 'description', provide text in Markdown format; on Jira Cloud, use '{expand:Title}...{expand}' for a collapsible section. Example: '{"assignee": "user@example.com", "summary": "New Summary", "description": "## Updated\nMarkdown text"}'

additional_fields.description: (Optional) JSON string of additional fields to update. Use this for custom fields or more complex updates. Link to epic: {"epicKey": "EPIC-123"} or {"epic_link": "EPIC-123"}.

attachments.description: (Optional) JSON string array or comma-separated list of file paths to attach to the issue. Example: '/path/to/file1.txt,/path/to/file2.txt' or ['/path/to/file1.txt','/path/to/file2.txt']

return_fields.description: (Optional) Controls which fields of the updated issue are returned, to reduce response size and token usage. Defaults to '*all' (the complete issue, which can be very large). TOKEN-SAVING TIP: after an update you usually do NOT need the whole issue back. Pass a comma-separated list of just the field(s) you care about (e.g., 'summary,duedate'), or a single light field such as 'status' for a minimal confirmation - this can cut the response by thousands of tokens. The issue 'key' is always returned regardless. If you later need other fields, fetch them on demand with jira_get_issue (which also supports field filtering). Use '*all' only when you genuinely need the full updated issue.
